# Open Dataset in R session:


## Using real IMPACT data

You can either load the dataset using a parquet extract from the IMPACT dataset as below

```{r, eval=FALSE}

# Load real data
impact <- IMPACTfunctions::load_dataset(folder_path = "~/data/dwhitake/data/IMPACT/20260624",
             prefix = "Periop_",
             suffix ="",
             verbose = FALSE,
             dictionary_check=TRUE)

# The dataset is returned as an object, so you can reach the tables through it
impact$Procedures

```

`load_dataset()` also attaches each table to your session by name, so
`Procedures`, `HospitalMar` and the rest can be used directly - this is what the
functions in this package expect by default. Pass `attach = FALSE` if you would
rather keep everything inside the returned object, and use `attach_dataset()` to
attach it later.

## Using synthetic data

Alternatively you can use the synthetic data that comes with the package to test and build your workflow whislt you wait for data. 
Note that the synthetic data is a minimum viable dataset to allow all of the functions within the package. The Fully IMPACT dataset can and does contain more data that we have not replicated. 

```{r, message=FALSE}
#If you do not have a real dataset, load the synthetic dataset
synth_data <- load_synthetic_dataset()
attach_dataset(synth_data)
rm(synth_data)

```

# A Note on package terminology

We use the following terms to describe our functions.

> Package Terminology
>
> Below is the prefixes and general purpose of each function family
> - `cohort_...()` - General functions to filter the whole extract to the population of intrest.
> - `cohort_enforce_...()` - Specific functions to filter one aspect, there are used in sequence for the `cohort_...()` functions.
> - `extract_...()` - Feature generation functions to extract a vector of the variables of intrest for a population.
> - `extract_record_...()` - Extract a single value from a single record, this function will be looped over within the respective `compute_...()` function. 

Note as a number of our extract functions are vectorised they may not have a extract_record version. Otherwise you should subset your dataframe to the patient of interest and then run the extract function. 


# Filtering the dataset to get study cohort

We might want a study cohort (or population of intrest more broadly) with a range of inclusion and exclusion criteria. 

## `cohort_...()` - General functions

We can use the general functions `cohort_...()` to produce these and tweak the arguments to produce our study population. 

```{r, echo=FALSE}
rm(eligibility_criteria)
```

### `cohort_complete_admissions()` - Return the procedures with complete data 
```{r}
dataset_1 <- cohort_complete_admissions(procedures_table = Procedures, verbose=TRUE)

#Use the glimpse function to peer into the dataset

dataset_1 %>% glimpse()

# Use the collect statement to call the table into the session memory as a dataframe

df <- dataset_1 %>% collect()

# View the eloigability criteria table to understand the filtering

eligibility_criteria
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
rm(eligibility_criteria)
rm(df)
rm(dataset_1)
```

### `cohort_procedure_codes()` - Return the procedures matching specific OPCS codes

```{r}

tonsillectomy <- cohort_procedure_codes(Procedures, cohort_name = "Tonsillectomy", include_OPCS = c("F34", "F35"))

df <- tonsillectomy %>% collect()

```

```{r}
#Use single `cohort_enforce` statements
dataset <- Procedures %>% cohort_enforce_opt_out(verbose=TRUE) 

#Or chain together multiple enforce statements
dataset <- Procedures %>% cohort_enforce_discharged(verbose=TRUE) %>%
  cohort_enforce_procedure_coded(verbose=TRUE, add_to_eligability_criteria = FALSE)

#Use the help to see the family of cohort_enforce functions
?cohort_enforce_family

```

```{r}

#Use the collect function to pull the dataset into memory as a dataframe
dataset_df <- dataset %>% collect()
```

Examine the eligibility criteria used in the filtering
```{r}
#See the eligibility criteria that has been applied
print(eligibility_criteria)

```
